text:
alex: Quick sanity-check — after the anchor-sequence change I can repro a replay mismatch where tokens after the anchor diverge on quant builds. Steps I used: prefill 2048 tokens, anchor=512, continue 200 tokens. First ~512 after continuation match, then divergence. Anyone seen this? @marta @jin

marta: I think I saw a similar pattern on the dynamic-padding run. Do you have a minimal repro we can run?

alex: Minimal script below, hits it locally against an internal endpoint. Using model redwood-v2-small-quant and 'prefill_anchor' flag.

```python
# repro: anchor-sequence replay mismatch
import requests
payload = {
  "model": "redwood-v2-small-quant",
  "prefill_anchor": 512,
  "input": "A" * 2048,
  "generate": 200
}
s = requests.Session()
r = s.post("https://internal-api.local/generate", json=payload, timeout=30)
print(r.json().get("tokens", [])[:560][-10:])
```

alex: I also dumped the KV snapshots around the boundary; sha256 of the dump: abc123def456... divergence observed starting at overall token idx 1026.

jin: Can you paste the KV key/index entries around 1020-1030? My gut says RoPE index scaling is applied with absolute positions somewhere it should be relative to anchor. That would explain anchor-dependent drift.

sam: I ran the same repro on fp32 and int8 builds. fp32: perfect match. int8: diverges after 512. Logs excerpt: 

```
[run] prefill=2048 anchor=512 mode=int8
[kv] shard0 idx=511->512 ok
[kv] shard1 idx=1023->1024 checksum mismatch (expected 0x9a12, got 0x8f34)
```

ml-ci-bot: test/anchor-replay (int8) failed — 1 mismatch. See job: https://ci.internal/job/anchor-replay/3421

marta: That points to quant packing/tiling. Try toggling runtime flag preserve_pos_offset — I remember an earlier change that rewrites pos indices during compact packing.

alex: I flipped preserve_pos_offset=true locally and re-ran. int8 now matches through whole 2048 in my quick run. So the rewrite path is the likely culprit.

jin: I'll add a fuzz suite that varies anchor offsets and sequence lengths. Proposed test matrix: anchors=[0,1,16,512,1023], lengths=[512,1024,2048,4096], and rotary_scale=[1.0,0.5]. Also include both int8 and fp32 branches.

sam: Actionable: set preserve_pos_offset default back to true in runtime until we root-cause and fix the packing logic. I'll open a PR with rollback and a test toggle.

alex: Good. Also we should add a KV checksum assert in apply_kv that fails loudly when a shard checksum changes unexpectedly (instead of silently drifting tokens).

marta: Agreed. Silent drift is dangerous. I'll prototype an assertion and a small regression test that compares fp32 vs quant outputs across anchors.

jin: I'll own the extended CI tests and add the fuzz cases. Will also instrument a short script to dump pos indices and ropescale factors at prefill boundary.

sam: I'll file the PR and add a note to the release for dedicated clusters. We should also run the repro across dedicated dev and the dedicated staging pool.

alex: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups: @jin add tests, @sam open PR + run on dedicated, @marta add assertion/regression. I'll queue the failing CI job with the repro artifacts so it's easier to debug.

marta: One more thought — if we keep preserve_pos_offset true, we should add a microbench to ensure we didn't regress throughput. If packing path was faster we might be trading perf for correctness temporarily.

alex: Noted — will measure perf on the PR pipeline.
